scope: Four extension/skill verification items; current-client/product and benefit acceptance remain open

observed: Native skill discovery publishes only name/description/source metadata; selected bodies are loaded on demand from host-selected directories with authority and file-policy checks. Five native skill tests include denied file/frontmatter and invalid-directory cases.
Product skill/discovery tests exercise loading and discovery behavior rather than inferring it from file presence.
remaining: Current-client browsing, explicit invocation, source/enabled-state presentation and conflict/incompatibility explanation still require an interaction matrix.
These fixtures do not measure whether model skill selection reduces task cost or avoids excess resource loading on a real task baseline.

observed: Compact disclosure offers bounded literal tool_search and stable top-level tool definitions. Catalog tests cover exact matching, bounded result schemas and unchanged stable surface.

MCP list_changed coalesces a 500ms refresh; fixtures cover catalog changes, reconnect/cancellation behavior and retaining a previous catalog after failed refresh. Registration/authority metadata binds grants.
remaining: Connection registration still fetches complete tool schema pages (bounded to four pages and 128 tools), rather than loading only the schemas selected by a very large catalog query. Model disclosure savings do not establish host-side lazy schema loading.
An explicit cache TTL/staleness and permission-change invalidation contract, plus current-client visibility, needs acceptance; list_changed refresh alone is not that whole contract.

observed: Product OAuth provider exposes CIMD metadata URLs, pre-registered and stored/dynamic client information, pending-token commit and issuer attribution. Callback tests reject a mismatching issuer and explicitly accept matching or absent iss.
Native HTTP fixtures cover host-provisioned refresh-token exchange, explicit generic failures, header authority, no credential-forwarding redirects and grants tied to registration metadata.
remaining: The native refresh-grant path delegates browser registration/discovery to the host; it is not a complete Rust-owned login workflow.
Fixture coverage does not establish the live authorization-server matrix across CIMD, pre-registration, dynamic registration and manual setup.
Current-client login, enable/disable, tool cancellation/reconnection and issuer-scoped grant reuse/rotation need live acceptance with supported servers.

observed: Native fixtures exercise LSP query validation, hover/definition/reference responses, edited-document diagnostics and read-triggered warmup. Formatter tests run after write/edit/patch and retain the final fingerprint even on timeout.
